nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

nodes.entity_id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
nodes.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages.
nodes.id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

nodes.description: A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and store first classification data in a persistent store; it may execute on a network device distinct from a client device.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that sorts messages into different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of user action.
A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, use it in a second pass to identify misclassified messages, and purge the model from non-persistent memory.
A model generated during the first pass analysis that resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and is used to score and identify misclassified messages.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it can be deleted so that it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and is deleted upon providing the display of information.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter may be configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform multi-pass message filtering actions.<SEP>A device that receives messages, assigns them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicates the messages over a network to the message folders.

A device on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may occur entirely, and on which the first pass is executed.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.<SEP>A device that executes the passes of the multi-pass message filter, holds second classification data in a non-persistent memory store, and provides a display of information about misclassified messages.

A storage medium storing instructions that, when executed, perform operations including the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass message filter.
An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed so misclassified messages can be moved to different folders.
A memory-resident-only location where the classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

An email message containing sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments, sorted into folders and analyzed by the filters.<SEP>A communication item received in plurality, sorted into message folders, and scored by the multi-pass message filter to identify incorrect folder sorting.

An address book associated with a recipient that may be analyzed to determine whether a message sender's address is present when generating the classification model.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

A message filtering method that executes a first pass and a second pass, can employ a Naive Bayes classifier, and is trained by generating second classification data.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
A classifier that the multi-pass message filter may employ.
A generated classification model produced based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.

One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted, and whose contents may be analyzed to generate the second classification model.<SEP>One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted; a message may be identified as stored in an incorrect message folder and moved to another folder.

A method for managing message delivery that includes receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on a client device.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.
A communications network over which the network device communicates messages to the message folders.
A header of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to indicate whether the message is sorted into an incorrect message folder.
